$comment: THE test manifest. Every test file on disk must appear here exactly once, and every entry
here must exist on disk — test/run.mjs --guard fails the build on either mismatch. This file
is the answer to "what is the suite?". Before it existed that question had no answer, and 35
of 144 test files had never run in CI: a test that is not wired in looks exactly like a test
that passes, because both are silent.
default      runs on every npm test. This is the release gate.
extended     correct but slow or heavy. Run deliberately, not on every commit.
integration  needs real WebRTC, a live bridge, or the network. Not hermetic, not a gate.
quarantined  KNOWN UNRUN, awaiting triage. A debt with a number attached, never a resting
place: the guard prints the count on every run so it cannot go quiet. Each
entry must say why it is here and what would resolve it.
retired      deliberately not run, with a recorded reason. A decision, not a drift.

tests.note: Q1 — requestPull must distinguish response/empty-response/timeout/invalid-response instead of collapsing all four to null. Verified RED against the pre-fix tree (empty, timeout and malformed were all null and indistinguishable). Drives the real requestPull + _onPullResp path; nothing stubbed.

Q2/C4 — a root's replica ledger records dispatch EVIDENCE, not a call that failed to throw. routeMessage reports failure by RESOLVING {consumed:false}, so consumed:false and async rejection must never credit a replica. v4.58.0 REWROTE section 3 to the inverse of what it first asserted: an adapter that returns no verdict credits NOTHING, whether it declared verdictsSupported (contract violation, loud) or declared it cannot report (honest, still no evidence). Capability is declared, never inferred — the original 'unreported still credits' let test doubles set a production durability semantic, and both reviewers rejected the inference itself. Verified RED. Drives the real _syncPush/_route chain; only the transport's answer varies.

Q2 point 6 — capability is DECLARED at construction, once and loudly, or the peer does not build. v4.58.0 first made a missing declaration a per-send 'violation': fail-closed, but an adapter that never declares would log one ERROR per message forever while staying silently uncreditable — a log storm standing in for a build error. Now a TypeError at construction. Truthiness is not a declaration: a string, number, null or object all still throw, because guessing at the shape is the thing being removed. Both booleans construct — 'false' must stay a first-class, unpunished answer, since it is what every honest non-reporting adapter says. Turning the throw on cost an audit of all 82 test doubles by what routeMessage actually RESOLVES: 2 declare true (one returns {consumed:true}, one delegates to the real AxonaPeer.routeMessage), 80 declare false. Blanket-declaring true to silence the throw would have converted every send from a non-reporting double into a violation and masked the regressions those tests exist to catch — the 'make the doubles pass' mistake with the sign flipped.

Q2 blocker 2 — the fail-closed CONFIRM GATE must ACT on its evidence, not merely count it. Drives the REAL root ingress with real Ed25519-signed envelopes (buildEnvelope + verifyEnvelope + checkFreshness + a topic id DERIVED from the descriptor + write policy + stamp + gate); section 0 asserts the ingress ACCEPTED the message so a later 'not confirmed' means WITHHELD and never DROPPED. FOUND THE DEFECT IT WAS WRITTEN FOR: _ingestPublish called _deliverToApp before the gate and _deliverToApp confirms, so a publisher subscribed to its own topic — the only way to verify a publish, since there is deliberately no publish-ack — confirmed regardless of cohort dispatch. Fixed by splitting DELIVERY from DURABILITY into two independent state machines (src/pubsub/durability.js) per Aster's council spec. Also caught a missing meta.isTerminal that had the kill checks asserting against a handler that returned early. Section 3 MOVED to fence_handoff_two_node.mjs, which is where the heir's ack can actually come back.

Aster's fourth Q2 requirement: a departing root's retry EXEMPTION must be earned. Two real managers and a real routing fabric, because _handoffAcked is populated by _onHandoffAck — a wire ACK from the HEIR — and a single-node harness has no heir to send one, so the consumed control there could never fire (measured: three pubsub:handoff dispatched {consumed:true}, set still empty). Proves the control FIRES when a live heir acks AND genuinely holds the history; that no ack means no exemption (#340: a leaver dropping the last copy and reporting success); and that an ack reporting held < sent earns nothing (#402) — someone replying is not the same as history surviving, which is this version's defect in one more costume.

CRASH SAFETY, not durability. v4.57.0 made _syncPush/_route return the transport promise; 13 fire-and-forget callers plus _send dropped it, and Node >=15 terminates on an unhandled rejection. Drives pubsubLeaveHandoff with a rejecting transport at both the root HANDOFF and last-gasp sites, asserts zero unhandledRejection and unchanged ACK/no-claim semantics. Includes a control that the harness itself detects an unhandled rejection. Requested by Aster+Orion (council 2026-07-31); found the exposure was the whole call graph, not the two sites diagnosed.

READ PATH, same defect family as Q2 — an obligation discharged on DISPATCH rather than arrival. _upstream pins a subscriber to the relay it renews toward, and until v4.58.0 only pubsubPeerDied (which needs a direct CHANNEL to the dead peer) or role teardown could drop it. A relay reached through routing could die unseen: the SUB exhausted in the mesh, _emitSubscribe stamped lastRenewSent anyway, and the pin outlived its target forever — worse, `attached` stayed true so the adaptive interval BACKED OFF toward RENEW_MS while reaching nobody. Only a reload recovered it (fresh peer, empty _upstream). Diagnosed by David from a wedged axona.chat window, 2026-08-01. Pins that an explicit routing failure — and ONLY an explicit routing failure, never a non-reporting adapter's silence — drops the pin and resets the renewal clock exactly as pubsubPeerDied does. Verified RED (pin survived, next SUB still carried the dead waypoint). Section 4 bounds the re-home against the unbounded-spin class that took the east bridge down on 2026-07-27.

WRITE PATH sibling of fence_subscribe_unpin — the corpse-defer family, opposite path. Pins the C+D unified transition (council 2026-08-02, seq 146/147 + the atNode amendment) and option B: (1) PUB/KILL forward to a beaconed root is a PROBE — dispatch first, mutate role/_upstream only on consumed AND atNode === the named root; consumed-elsewhere or absent atNode mutates NOTHING (organic DELIVER re-homes). (2) A failed probe invalidates ONLY the matching beacon record (identity + at guard) so the publisher own early-resend retries root properly — no demote, no pin; pre-fix, _deferToRoot demoted and re-pinned BEFORE the send, so one publish handed to a dead relay both vanished (consumed) and converted a working read path into a starved one. (3) The verified-beacon bypass gets the 1.5xBEACON_MS freshness cut — it had NO liveness test and NO freshness cut, 90s life, and captured SUB too. Section 3 drives the PRODUCTION writer (_verifyRoots) per Aster review, not only an injected record. Controls keep the anti-hotspot last-mile correction alive: reachable closer root still wins the forward, multi-hop live root that CONSUMES the probe still re-homes us (the case that made strict reachability wrong), farther node never (I-2). Verified RED 10/28 against 99a9b55, GREEN 28/28 with the fix. Provenance: the 2026-08-02 prod write outage — ~20 relays lost to a host restart, reads fine, writes dead for hours with 6/8 holders alive.

THIRD member of the corpse family — the zombie-neighbour window. Fact-finding instrument for the 2026-08-07 prod specimen (GH #28): an ungracefully-killed root (no leave, no channel close) stays in dht.neighbors() until the transport evicts it, and _isReachableId — the one clause of liveCloserRoot with NO freshness cut — keeps returning the corpse from the 30 s freshness cut to the record TTL (50 s plain / 90 s verified), on strict AND loose gates, while _topicDecision keeps routing writes toward it and the closest LIVE node declines to root. Sections 1 and 3 pin the DEFECT AS IT STANDS (deliberately green pre-fix; they FLIP to the fixed contract when Dead-Root Eviction v0.2, council-ratified 2026-08-07, ships — see evict/E5). Section 2 is the clean-departure control and stays green forever. MEASURED BOUND worth remembering: one record cannot outlive 90 s, so the 50-minute specimen strand additionally requires active state regeneration — this fence documents the window, not the regeneration; that question stays open on GH #28.

Dead-Root Eviction v0.3 phase E1 — root incarnation plumbing. Every entry to ROOT mints epoch = _knownEpoch(topic)+1 (both sites: rootClaim.become born-as-root and rootClaim._set promotion flip); beacons carry `epochs` index-aligned with `topics`; receivers store it as a HIGH-WATER MARK on the beacon record (lower later epochs never regress it, garbage reads as 0); a beacon without the field interoperates as epoch 0 both directions. Epoch ORDERS claims for a seat — no placement behavior changes in E1; comparison semantics land with epoch reconciliation (E4) and eviction tombstones join _knownEpoch's max in E3.

Dead-Root Eviction v0.3 phase E2 — the typed INGEST-ack. A root emits {topicId, msgId, epoch, op} ONE HOP back to the forwarder (meta.fromId) after topic-store ingest, never at routing and never to the origin publisher (no publish-ack: location privacy; the E3 write flight lives at the deferral sites). PUB completes on ingest, KILL completes separately on tombstone ingest with the TARGET msgId bound; duplicates ack again (idempotent-retry success — an ack is what stops the flight from probing a root doing its job); verification drops (tampered signature, unparseable body) ack NOTHING. _ingestPublish now returns typed {ok, msgId, reason} — the replicate-all-failed path still acks ok (ingest happened; durability is the cohort's job and the tick retries it independently, v0.3 'death immediately after ingest-ack'). Receiver side (_onIngestAck) records correlations in a 512-bounded insertion-ordered store for the E3 flight; malformed ops record nothing. Real Ed25519 envelopes through the real ingress, fence_q2 harness discipline.

Write-Flight Ack Routing v0.9 (4.62.2) D1 + Aster R7 — the signed INGEST-ACK proof (src/pubsub/ackProof.js), the deaf-flight fix's cryptographic core. Byte-exact transcript: DOMAIN 'AXONA_INGEST_ACK_PROOF_V1' (25) + u8(purpose) + u8(op) + topicId(33) + msgId(32) + u64(epoch) + attemptId(16) + ackTo(33) + flightNonce(16) + rootPub(32) = 197 bytes fixed. Checked-in GOLDEN vector (fixed secret 01..20 + fixed inputs -> exact signature) that an independent impl must reproduce. Rejection vectors: NACK-relabeled-as-ACK fails on the signed purpose byte (R7); tampered msgId / flipped op / wrong-width attemptId+rootPub / valid-sig-under-a-different-key all fail; purpose outside the closed set is refused by the builder. Authority binding (R1, refined): rootPub binds to the HASH PORTION of the flight's rootHex (SHA-256(rootPub) & HASH_MASK) since the region prefix is not key-derivable — region-independent, same security property. Pure module, no transport.

Write-Flight Ack Routing v0.9 (4.62.2) — Aster fixed-slice review. The signed D1 proof must round-trip under a SHRUNK keyspace profile (hashBits:64, HEX_CHARS=18) AND an ODD canonical-width profile (hashBits:66, HEX_CHARS=19), using the REAL idHex() serializer. Pins Aster's blocking finding: idHex() pads every id to 66 hex / 33 bytes UNCONDITIONALLY in every profile, so proof topicId/ackTo are a fixed ID_BYTES=33 — the transcript builder enforces exactly that (not HEX_CHARS/2, which rejected the real signed path under a shrunk profile). Asserts idHex length 66 under both profiles, a signed proof over idHex-produced ids verifies, and a raw shrunk-width id (bypassing idHex) is still refused on width. Restores hashBits:256 at end.

Write-Flight Ack Routing v0.9 (4.62.2) D0 selector — AxonaManager.pickCapableAdjacent(topicBig) returns the topic-closest ADJACENT peer with attested write-flight-ack capability, or null → the D0 observation-only fallback. Reads dht.isCapable(peerHex) (the transport's per-channel flag set from a verified CAP_ATTEST). Cases: all-capable picks closest; a closer incapable peer is skipped for the next capable; none-capable → null; adapter without isCapable → null (fail-closed, so sim doubles / pre-4.62.2 transports never yield a false delegate); self excluded; no neighbours → null. The transport CAP_ATTEST exchange that sets isCapable is the follow-on wiring.

Write-Flight Ack Routing v0.9 (4.62.2) R13/R15/R17 — the authenticated capability oracle (src/pubsub/capAttest.js), the byte-exact contract D0 uses to pick a 4.62.2-capable adjacent delegate. Transcript: DOMAIN 'AXONA_CAP_ATTEST_V1' (19) + u8(19) + capId 'write-flight-ack-v1' (19) + nodeId (33) + cbvDigest (32) = 104 bytes; checked-in GOLDEN signature. cbvDigest = SHA-256(UTF-8(currentTransportCbvString)) verified against an independent SHA-256 and against node-WS/bridge/mesh CBV-string fixtures. R15 key binding: the frame carries no pubkey — verifyCapAttest checks the sig ONLY against the base-authenticated peerKey passed by the channel, so a claim signed by a different identity fails and an extra key field on the frame is ignored (wrong peerKey still fails). R17 freshness: a prior-channel frame replayed with a different current cbvString fails (verifier derives a different digest — no nonce table). Plus nodeid-mismatch, wrong-capId, and missing-peerKey fail-closed. Pure module; transport wiring + pickCapableAdjacent land with D0.

Write-Flight Ack Routing v0.9 (4.62.2) D1 — the deaf-flight fix proven at the manager seam. An owner opens a flight; the root signs an ACK PROOF; the proof delivered from a RELAY that is NOT the root (the last-hop case #51 dropped) still completes the flight, because _flightCompleteSigned binds the verified proof to the owner's flight by attemptId + ackTo + flightNonce + hash-bound root authority, never the last hop (meta.fromId is a non-root relay throughout). Negatives: a proof from the wrong identity (authority mismatch), a wrong flightNonce, a wrong attemptId, and (case 6, REF-0.2 seq-598 #3) a valid proof addressed to a DIFFERENT same-width ackTo all leave the flight OPEN for receipt-bound recovery; a correct proof then completes it. The destination-binding case is distinct from the wrong-WIDTH ackTo rejection in smoke_ack_proof — here the proof is well-formed and validly signed but over a different legitimate destination. Case 7 (REF-0.2 v0.4, Aster REF-0.2-v0.3 disposition) is the duplicate signed-ACK ingest smoke_ack_proof does NOT provide: the SAME valid proof redelivered settles the flight exactly once, every repeat is an idempotent no-op, and _writeFlights (the only correlation store) resurrects no flight and does not grow. 16 assertions total. Threads the transport identity into AxonaManager; _forwardToRoot/_flightOpen stamp ackTo+flightNonce+attemptId; _sendIngestAck signs when identity+ackTo present else 4.62.1 unsigned one-hop; _onIngestAck verifies + routes to _flightCompleteSigned.

Refactor Phase 1 REF-1.1 S1..S1i — shadow frame-contract registry CORE in isolation (src/registry/; relocated out of src/pubsub in S2.0a as the boundary-neutral shared reflection-safety core all four registries consume). Hardened across nine adversarial review rounds through Aster's S1i clearance (Option B trust boundary: intact realm intrinsics for the certify-and-dispatch lifetime). 89 assertions (S2.0c §10: the fixed per-variant certifying decoders certifyPlain/certifyBigint reusing the transport bigintReviver; input-type normalization; the F7 pre-parse UTF-8-BYTE ceiling owned by the transport contract wire.js MAX_FRAME_BYTES — an INVARIANT hard cap a caller may only tighten (a supplied cap above it, or otherwise invalid, REJECTS), with omitted-vs-explicit-undefined arity enforced via arguments.length so only a genuinely omitted cap defaults; the MAX_NODES adversarial-breadth brand-loss demonstration; and §10j, a Finding-2 TRIPWIRE proving a legitimate full-state REPLICATE frame (built via wire.encode) EXCEEDS the PROVISIONAL 1 MiB cap — the cap value is pending the chunk-vs-ceiling design decision, so 1 MiB is NOT justified and this assertion must be revisited when that lands). Invariants: flag OFF verbatim pass-through (value/this/ALL-args/throw; zero trace); flag ON validate+trace never alters verdict; OBSERVATION ISOLATION via a bounded reference-disjoint deeply-frozen projection of ONLY declared fields (non-scalars never exposed; nested live objects untouched; no shared graph on any path); fully-contained faults — throwing enabled()/sink/then-getter/consumed-getter/selector never reach the handler; selector output validated to null|bounded-string (no coercion trap); non-forgeable WeakSet brand (forged rows rejected); duplicate/unknown-variant resolve no contract; defineRow strict validation (integer version bounds+ordering, string guards, array fields, unique correlationFields, positive budgets, REQUEST_RESPONSE⇒correlation, COMMITTED⇒producedPolicy); telemetry bounded + registry-declared only (variant clamped, correlation kind = declared subjectShape not callback, no payload/hash values); 1-of-N sampling with faults always emitted. Pure-additive, nothing wired to live dispatch yet (that is S2).

REF-0.2 golden trace #1 (Aster seq-598) — reorder convergence of the stamped-set materialization at the TopicStore seam. The SAME set of signed, already-stamped bodies (the replicate / replay-up / handoff shape carrying its own publishTs+seq) plus one authorized kill, ingested via the real _ingestStamped + _applyKill in four arrival orders (in-order, reversed, kill-before-target, shuffled). CONVERGES order-independently: the held msgId SET, high-water cursor (lastTs -> _highWater, the `since` a renewal advertises), the dense seq counter, the tombstone set, and the survivors' exactly-once app delivery — a kill suppresses its target whether it arrives before or after the body. CHARACTERIZES two arrival-ordered facts the refactor must own: (1) low-water is cache[0].publishTs and the cache is stored in arrival order, so _lowWater is NOT convergent — the seam requirement that TopicStore keep a stamp-ordered structure; asserting current behavior makes a future stamp-ordered store break exactly this one check. (2) the killed body's app-delivery TIMELINE — delivered-then-retracted iff it arrived before its kill, suppressed otherwise — while the durable state a late joiner replays still converges. No wire, no kernel change; drives the store transition directly with _rootReplicas unset so the eager-replicate branch stays out.

Write-Flight Ack Routing v0.9 (4.62.2) R13/R15/R17 integration — the CAP_ATTEST exchange wired into MeshAuth over the in-memory data-channel loopback, the live oracle on the p2p path. After base auth binds a channel, each side captures the AUTHENTICATED peer pubkey + the channel's own CBV string, signs a capAttest frame (signCapAttest over st.cbv), and the peer verifies it against that base-authenticated key + its own cbv (R15 key binding / R17 freshness derived locally, no nonce table) → MeshAuth.isCapable(meshId) flips true and onCapable(peerNodeId, meshId) fires. Honest bidirectional exchange makes both sides capable; a peer that never attests is never marked capable (fail-closed, asymmetry allowed); onChannelLost clears the per-channel flag (never persisted). Drives the real MeshAuth FSM; the loopback route dispatches hello/hello-sig/cap-attest. The webTransport/node/bridge frame dispatch + AxonaPeer isCapable surfacing that feed dht.isCapable are the follow-on wiring.

Dead-Root Eviction v0.3 phase E3 — the write recovery flight. A forwarded PUB/KILL completes ONLY on its correlated INGEST-ack; consumed-at-the-named-root stays hop-local evidence (2a is the direct assertion against the GH #28 captured mode). Centerpiece: RESPONSIVE-NO-MUTATION (Aster seq 427) — a root that answers everything (attributed verdicts, probe NACKs) while producing no receipt is evicted on the bounded rounds cap, its incarnation tombstoned {root, epoch}, its beacon buried, and the write retry-promoted via-pinned to the closest LIVE holder whose own terminal machinery roots+ingests+acks (promotion IS the existing closest-live rule; a second flapper gets a fresh flight). Also: silence/SIGKILL analog convicts on probe-window expiry; serialization (two stranded writers join ONE flight, one probe); promotion-to-SELF when no neighbour lives, minting epoch PAST the tombstone (the E4 epoch chain seeded); the tombstone gates the corpse's ghost beacon at epoch<=conviction and admits a HIGHER-epoch rebirth. Flights swept from refreshTick — no per-flight timers; every exit deletes the flight (1c/2i assert empty maps). v4.62.1 (Aster seq 439 correctness block): the ack must BIND — _flightComplete enforces sender===the flight's suspect root AND epoch===the intended incarnation (unversioned epoch-0 flights, the post-eviction promotion case, accept the right node's first ack); section 9 pins the negatives — a different holder's valid ack and the right node at the wrong epoch both leave the flight open and recovery proceeds.

Dead-Root Eviction v0.3 phase E4 — adopt-on-rejoin + epoch-ordered reconciliation. Root claims for one seat converge by a TOTAL order: (1) a returning tombstoned root — typically the CLOSEST node — adopts under a farther promoted root whose epoch supersedes its own; the higher-epoch beacon passes the closeness accept-gate specifically so the one corrective beacon is not discarded, and the demote is attributed 'epoch-superseded'. (2) A closer but CONVICTED claim — its incarnation tombstoned by the E3 flight — never takes the seat; a mere epoch lag is NOT a conviction (the first draft rejected any lower epoch and broke ordinary succession, caught by smoke_split_history_union: a legitimate closer newcomer lags by construction when it minted before hearing the incumbent). Epochs order ADOPTION; tombstones order REJECTION. (3) Ordinary succession — closer AND higher — behaves as always. (4) Wire compat both directions: whenever EITHER side is unversioned (epoch 0, a pre-epoch build), the standing closeness rule is the whole rule, so mixed-version meshes behave exactly as 4.61.x — a versioned beacon does not bulldoze an unversioned root, and an unversioned closer claimant still wins.

C4 (partial) — a root must not record a cohort member in role.replicas when the push to it threw. Verified RED against the pre-fix code (1b/2b fail, replicas=2). Pins the LEDGER only; what discharges the ROOT obligation is the open C4 decision and sync.lastFullAt is deliberately not asserted.

tests.note: Aster CHANGES-REQUIRED on df41e05 (council 2026-08-01): durability.js shipped an attempt budget, an `expired` terminal and a module comment describing a lifecycle that DID NOT RUN. record() was called at exactly one site — the eager replicate inside the `role.isRoot && this._rootReplicas` gate — and _replicateRoots was fire-and-forget, so no periodic result reached the ledger: an entry that started verified:0 stayed pending forever, `expired` was unreachable, and rootReplicas:0 never recorded at all. I had written the intent as though it were the implementation. This file asserts the lifecycle by EXECUTION: rootReplicas:0 reaches an explicitly chosen terminal (expired / 'no-replication-configured'); initially-failed-then-consumed reaches VERIFIED via the periodic path; repeated failure reaches EXPIRED exactly at DURABILITY_ATTEMPTS (asserted against the exported constant, not a magic number); leave() observes terminal state with the undurable count retained rather than clearing a stall.

Aster's fourth Q2 requirement, on the branch that implements it — fence_handoff_two_node claimed this and tested the ROOT path instead (its pair() calls _becomeRoot). Drives repairPlane's leave-handoff REPLICATE leg, where there is NO ack and the dispatch verdict is the only evidence, so a wrong answer is least visible and most expensive: a departing holder that exempts itself stops retrying and the last copy leaves with it (#340). Exemption is GRANTED only on explicit consumed; REFUSED for explicit failure, rejection, declared-false/void and declared-true/void. Verified RED against the pre-fix negative test (dispatchVerdict !== 'failed'): the two void cases flip to exempt. Section 0c pins the liveness gate and states why every case hides the root — my first draft left the principal in neighbors(), the holder correctly skipped the handoff, and all four refusals were VACUOUS at sent=[]; section 2a exists to catch exactly that.

Aster's third required control: an ACTUAL late-subscriber/retry regression for the killed unverified body, not cache/map assertions. fence_q2_end_to_end 5f-5i assert on _pendingPub/tombstones/cacheIds — right invariants, one layer above what matters — so this asks at the app callback of a REAL second node. Section 1 is the control (no kill, the late subscriber DOES receive it), without which 'received nothing' is also what a broken fabric produces. Section 4 records a correction to what I first wrote: I injected the reverted fix's regression (removed _pendingPub.delete from _confirmPending) and sections 2-3 stayed GREEN — the pump fired (6 pubsub:pub across 3 ticks) and tombstone-gated ingest refused every one. So section 4 disables the cancellation deliberately and requires the tombstone to hold alone. Verified RED: with the ingest tombstone gate off, the killed body is re-ingested (cache:1) and DELIVERED to the late subscriber, while sections 2-3 stay green.

Aster CHANGES-REQUIRED on 533116a (council 2026-08-01): the v4.58.1 periodic ledger hook fed recordTopic two results that are NOT evidence. (1) _replicateRole returns nil('deferred-no-budget') when the tick's full-push budget is spent — nothing sent, attempted:0 — and record() reads attempted===0 as 'no cohort exists' -> EXPIRED, so under load a message whose snapshot never reached the wire went permanently undurable because the tick was busy: fail-closed run backwards. (2) _replicateRole sends full:false when the signature is unchanged and replicas are credited — an EMPTY keepalive — which still resolves consumed and still counted verified>0, so recordTopic marked every pending message on the topic VERIFIED. Reachable in ordinary operation: a new message whose eager full push fails still writes role.sync.sig, so the next tick picks the keepalive. Root cause on my side: the v4.58.1 commit justified topic granularity with '_syncPush sends the role's whole snapshot' — true of a FULL push, written unconditionally. FIX: _replicateRole reports `dispatched` and `snapshot`; DurabilityLedger.recordTopic is fail-closed on both, at the LEDGER not the caller, because a rule enforced at one call site lasts until the second. Section 1 is unit-level with a positive control; sections 2 and 3 drive the real refreshTick sweep — 2c proves the deferral is real (budget spent on other roles, OUR topic sent nothing), 3d proves the keepalive really carried zero messages, and 3f/3g prove a later real snapshot still verifies, so the rule is 'only a full snapshot counts', not 'nothing counts'. Verified RED: 2d flips to expired and 3e flips to verified.
